_note: Published values used for comparison, transcribed from the sources below. Each entry records the model the number comes from (CR3BP or ephemeris). Read by scripts/make_results.py.

zimovan2017.citation: E. M. Zimovan, K. C. Howell, D. C. Davis, "Near Rectilinear Halo Orbits and Their Application in Cis-Lunar Space," 3rd IAA Conference on Dynamics and Control of Space Systems (DyCoSS), Moscow, 2017, paper IAA-AAS-DyCoSS3-125.
zimovan2017.model: CR3BP (Earth-Moon); values read from the paper's Figure 9, stated as approximate
zimovan2017.quote: a 4:1 synodic resonance, that occurs for an NRHO with perilune radius of about 5600 km ... A 3:1 synodic resonance occurs for an NRHO with perilune radius equal to approximately 15000 km, while the 9:2 resonant NRHO possesses a perilune radius of about 3150 km.

lee2019.citation: D. E. Lee, "White Paper: Gateway Destination Orbit Model: A Continuous 15 Year NRHO Reference Trajectory," NASA Johnson Space Center, August 20, 2019, NTRS 20190030294.
lee2019.model: Ephemeris (n-body point-mass gravity, 15-year reference trajectory with small velocity adjustments every revolution); NOT CR3BP
lee2019.quote: The resulting orbit has a perilune radius that varies from 3196 to 3557 km, with an average of 3366 km. The average orbit period of the reference trajectory is 6.562 days

folta2022.citation: D. Folta, N. Bosanac, I. Elliott, L. Mann, R. Mesarch, J. Rosales, "Astrodynamics Convention and Modeling Reference for Lunar, Cislunar, and Libration Point Orbits," NASA/TP-20220014814, Version 1.1, December 2022.
folta2022.note: Does not tabulate the 9:2 NRHO. Used for its system constants (Table 2) and its example Lyapunov and halo orbits (Table 3, values to 6 decimals).
